props.title: The Doctor

sections.content: The Doctor marked a pivotal moment in medical dramas by flipping the power dynamic - showing an arrogant surgeon becoming a patient himself. William Hurt delivers a masterful performance as Dr. Jack McKee, whose transformation echoes similar character arcs in Regarding Henry (1991) and Awakenings (1990). The film hit during a wave of early 90s medical dramas that included Article 99 (1992) and Lorenzo's Oil (1992), all examining healthcare through a deeply personal lens rather than just procedural drama.

sections.content: Director Randa Haines, who previously tackled disability awareness in Children of a Lesser God (1986), brings remarkable sensitivity to scenes of medical procedures and patient experiences. The film's emphasis on doctor-patient relationships influenced later works like Wit (2001) and Side Effects (2013), establishing a template for exploring medical ethics through character-driven narratives rather than melodrama.

What sets The Doctor apart is its unflinching look at medical culture itself. Unlike the more sanitized Patch Adams (1998), it critiques the emotional distance many doctors maintain from patients. This theme would later be explored differently in Something the Lord Made (2004) and Miss Evers' Boys (1997), both examining medical ethics through historical lenses. movies.title: Something the Lord Made
movies.slug: True story of a cardiac surgery pioneer and his Black lab technician who helped revolutionize heart surgery

sections.content: The film's influence extends beyond cinema into television, helping pave the way for more nuanced medical shows like ER and grittier hospital documentaries. Its exploration of medical hierarchy and patient dignity resonates with later works like Malice (1993) and Extreme Measures (1996), though few match its intimate portrayal of professional arrogance transformed through personal crisis.
